comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological framework (C29-C142). Both evaluate the phylogenetic approach as SUPPORTED, with reviewers praising it as 'solid' and 'distinctive,' specifically highlighting the GOE maximum constraint as 'novel and interesting.'

Strong disagreement on calibration strategy (C36-C42, C150-C152). OpenEval finds calibrations SUPPORTED with validation from prior-only analysis, but peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, calling the GOE maximum for aerobic groups 'an important mistake' due to pre-GOE oxygen evidence. Peer review also questions biogenic methane and crown Cyanobacteria calibration logic.

Partial overlap on sensitivity analyses (C145-C159). OpenEval finds validation tests SUPPORTED and notes consistency across methods strengthens confidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge these tests but remain UNCERTAIN, stating 'despite validation tests showing consistency, the fundamental calibration assumptions are contested.'

Disagreement on early clade dating (C3-C5, C45, C49-C51). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation connecting dates to GOE. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'uncertainty of many of the dates used to anchor ancient geological events' and stating 'further studies are needed.' Age estimates depend on contested calibrations.

Partial overlap on ecological interpretations (C46-C48, C52-C58). OpenEval finds OMZ refugia inference SUPPORTED though speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not directly challenging the interpretation but noting it depends on questioned age estimates from contested calibrations.

Both address limitations for specific clades (C59-C60). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging speculation about extinction/under-sampling cannot be tested. Peer reviewers include these claims in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of early clade dating affected by calibration concerns.

Disagreement on MGI/AOA dating (C8, C61-C65, C75). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with external validation and consistency across methods. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing conflicting study (Ren et al., 2019) suggesting pre-NOE diversification versus authors' later estimate (678 My).

Partial overlap on bacterial-eukaryotic connections (C66-C73). OpenEval finds temporal correlation SUPPORTED though causality cannot be definitively established. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not directly contesting the connection but noting foundational age estimates remain disputed.

Overlap on MGI mechanistic explanation (C76-C78). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers include in UNCERTAIN evaluation due to contested MGI age estimates, though the metabolic reasoning itself is not directly challenged.

Partial overlap on comparison with prior work (C160-C161). OpenEval notes SUPPORTED agreement with Yang et al. (2021) for MGI. Peer reviewers explicitly cite this as source of UNCERTAINTY, referencing conflicting Ren et al. (2019) study.

Disagreement on phototroph dating (C12-C13, C79-C82). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with agreement to independent studies and robustness across methods. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing conflicting Zhang et al. (2021) estimate of 800 My for Prochlorococcus versus authors' later diversification, noting 'further studies are needed.'

Partial overlap on oligotrophic ocean interpretation (C85-C94). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED connection between timing and oligotrophic productivity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not directly challenging interpretation but noting young clade ages 'remain uncertain relative to the broader literature.'

Minor overlap on established knowledge (C83-C84). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as appropriate context. Peer reviewers include in UNCERTAIN evaluation, though these background claims themselves are not contested.

Overlap on Prochlorococcus comparison (C162-C163). OpenEval notes SUPPORTED agreement with Sánchez-Baracaldo (2015). Peer reviewers acknowledge this agreement but rate UNCERTAIN due to conflict with Zhang et al. (2021), stating 'further studies are needed.'

Perfect agreement on stochastic mapping for EBC genes (C95-C104). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical validation and consistency with GOE hypothesis. Peer reviewers specifically praise 'gene content enrichment' as 'particularly novel and interesting.'

Perfect agreement on phycosphere gene enrichment (C105-C114). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds motility and vitamin metabolism genes support phycosphere hypothesis. Peer reviewers praise the gene content enrichment approach as novel, with no direct critiques of the interpretation.

Perfect agreement on phototroph gene patterns (C115-C124). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds transporter enrichment in Crocosphaera and minimal enrichment in Prochlorococcus consistent with known characteristics. Peer reviewers accept as part of praised functional genomic analysis.

Disagreement on Cyanobacteria calibration (C43-C44). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED validation by recovering expected lineages and agreement with Ward et al. (2016). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning why GOE is used as minimum for crown rather than stem, stating 'it seems a formal possibility that crown Cyanobacteria are younger than the GOE.'

Perfect agreement on climate change implications (C130-C134). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds inference about OMZs as ancient refugia and oligotrophic waters as modern well-supported. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting work 'will be of broad interest' to understanding modern ocean changes.

OpenEval evaluates stochastic mapping statistical methodology (C164-C168) as SUPPORTED with sound approach and appropriate null model. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates scientific context and motivation (C1-C2, C15-C28, C125-C127, C129) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and identification of knowledge gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these introductory claims.

Minor overlap on GOE context (C100). OpenEval rates established knowledge as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include C100 in SUPPORTED evaluation of stochastic mapping results showing enrichment consistent with GOE hypothesis.
